result.answer: Inner Monologue in Moshi refers to the mechanism whereby the model generates a textual representation of its own speech as a prefix to its semantic token stream, effectively modelling the transcription of its audio output with a text language model backbone (Helium) and using Whisper to obtain the transcription; this text stream is inserted before semantic token generation, providing scaffolding that improves linguistic quality and substantially boosts performance on spoken QA benchmarks while only slightly increasing inference cost [3c2cb5554c4aa008812c]. The architecture overview notes that time‑aligned text tokens are used for Moshi when employing Inner Monologue, linking speech and text generation in real time [40ef1cb89c86189e3a77]. Empirical results show that Inner Monologue nearly triples Moshi’s accuracy across benchmarks, highlighting its impact on both spoken question answering and overall linguistic quality [98171e126615a956d75c].

data-dependent dynamic chunking (DC) process (Figure 1). H-Nets match the efficiency of tokenized pipelines while

result.answer: The original Transformer does not rely on recurrent layers to capture token order; instead it adds explicit positional encodings to the input representations because the architecture contains no recurrence or convolution [1c951cef10022cbdda2d]. These sinusoidal encodings provide each position with a unique vector, enabling the model to attend to relative positions without sequential processing [a4cf5b02d4afd54c9738].

where pos is the position and i is the dimension. That is, each dimension of the positional encoding
corresponds to a sinusoid. The wavelengths form a geometric progression from 2π to 10000 · 2π. We
chose this function because we hypothesized it would allow the model to easily learn to attend by
relative positions, since for any fixed offset k, P Epos+k can be represented as a linear function of
P Epos.
We also experimented with using learned positional embeddings [9] instead, and found that the two

because it may allow the model to extrapolate to sequence lengths longer than the ones encountered
during training.

body.question: Why does the original Transformer require recurrent layers for positional encoding?

resource.question: Why does the original Transformer require recurrent layers for positional encoding?

result.answer: The original Transformer does not rely on recurrent layers because its architecture contains no recurrence or convolution, so to give the model a sense of token order it must inject positional information directly into the embeddings; this is done by adding sinusoidal positional encodings (or learned alternatives) to the input embeddings at the bottoms of the encoder and decoder stacks so that each position can be distinguished despite the lack of recurrence [946aec7000f086f6f07a].

citations.text:
Since our model contains no recurrence and no convolution, in order for the model to make use of the
order of the sequence, we must inject some information about the relative or absolute position of the
tokens in the sequence. To this end, we add "positional encodings" to the input embeddings at the
bottoms of the encoder and decoder stacks. The positional encodings have the same dimension dmodel
as the embeddings, so that the two can be summed. There are many choices of positional encodings,
learned and fixed [9].
In this work, we use sine and cosine functions of different frequencies:
